title: 2025-06-17-horizonbridge-private-network-constraints-discovery
summary: Intro discovery focused on private networking constraints for a regulated fintech. Discussed VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints, transit gateway, IP whitelisting, egress flow, and regional restrictions. Action items: share network diagram and IP ranges, provide SOC2 & KMS guidance, propose pilot plan for a single-region private deployment. Customer concerned about cross-region traffic, static egress IPs, and SOC2 audit evidence.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE); Priya Raman (Redwood SE); Sam Ortiz (CSM) — HorizonBridge: Tom Keller (VP Eng), Marta Ruiz (Cloud Architect), Jordan Lee (NetEng), Nadia Park (Security)

Auto-summary: quick discovery re: private/VPC deployment. Customer is regulated (payments), wants private-only traffic, static egress, and SOC2 evidence. Discuss high-level architecture tradeoffs.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Tom: good thanks alex, busy week but excited to dig in, we had a quick internal pre-read.
[00:12] Marta: hi all, this is Marta, i'll be the cloud arch lead on this. quick ask, we're trying to keep everything private — no internet egress from our pods if possible.
[00:20] Priya: understood, thanks Marta. just to set expectations we'll walk through options: private endpoints (privatelink-style), VPC peering, or transit-gateway patterns and what Redwood's private offering looks like.
[00:31] Jordan: quick one — we need static egress IPs, our firewall policies only allow specific IPs to reach 3rd party services. is that possible?
[00:38] Alex: yes, static egress is a common ask. for private we can provide documented egress IP ranges per region; need to confirm for dedicated vs hosted differences. i'll follow up with precise ranges.
[00:48] Nadia: and for compliance — SOC2 and KMS integration. do you support customer-managed keys?
[00:54] Priya: we do support KMS integrations for private deployments; on prem HSM is possible with our private package but need to map requirements. we'll share an integration note.
[01:05] Tom: good. also regional gating — some of our data must remain in eu-west-1, can't traverse us-east-1 even for inference. how strict are region restrictions?
[01:15] Priya: you can pin to a region for private deployments; Redwood Private offers region-scoped control, and we can ensure model serving stays in the chosen region. cross-region fallbacks by default are disabled unless you opt-in.
[01:28] Marta: what's the connectivity surface? do we do privatelink endpoints in our VPC and nodes call out to service, or peering? pros/cons?
[01:36] Priya: great question. brief summary — VPC peering is simpler for low-volume scenarios but scales poorly with many VPCs. Privatelink/private endpoints give you an endpoint network interface and stable private IPs per AZ; transit gateway is better if you have many VPCs/centralized routing. for high throughput we recommend direct peering or dedicated deployment in the same region with RGW — uh, sorry, Redwood dedicated pool.
[01:58] Jordan: latency wise — peering vs privatelink differences? we care about 50–150ms p95 budget end-to-end.
[02:05] Priya: peering has slightly lower hop count and typically lower latency. privatelink adds an extra hop through endpoint service but usually within a few ms. the key is avoiding public internet; both are private. we can run benchmarks during pilot.
[02:21] Sam: note — cost tradeoff: privatelink has per-GB data processing fees on the cloud side plus endpoint hours; peering may have cross-AZ or cross-region charges depending on topology.
[02:33] Tom: ideal architecture for us would be private endpoints from our VPC to Redwood in eu-west-1 for production and a staging small instance in us-west-2. does that create cross-region compliance issues?
[02:44] Nadia: yes mixing regions for production could flag auditors unless traffic is strictly segregated.
[02:49] Priya: you can do dual accounts or strict routing to ensure prod only talks to eu-west-1. we'll help with routing examples.
[02:57] Marta: can you accept connections from a peered VPC that uses AWS Transit Gateway? we use TGW as central hub.
[03:04] Priya: yes, TGW is supported but requires route table and permission configuration. some providers don't accept transitive routing by default; we'll share the exact requirements.
[03:15] Jordan: any IP address limits on the endpoint side? we need to plan subnets.
[03:20] Priya: endpoints consume ENIs per AZ; you'll want spare IPs in those subnets. we'll provide recommended /22 or /21 ranges depending on scale.
[03:30] Tom: firewalls — we have strict egress rules, our NATs are audited. does Redwood require outbound TLS to internet for anything?
[03:38] Alex: not for private deployments — the inference traffic is private. control plane calls may require connectivity to Redwood control plane if you pick managed control plane; however Private offers a customer-managed control plane option for air-gapped setups.
[03:52] Nadia: for audits we need logs and traceability. do you provide audit logs for API calls and model versions?
[03:58] Priya: yes we provide request-level logs and model versioning info; for Private we can push logs to your S3 or SIEM via Kinesis — we'll include an example.
[04:10] Tom: curious about fallback behavior — if dedicated capacity is full in eu-west-1 can requests failover to another region? we don't want that.
[04:18] Priya: by default Redwood won't failover across regions for pinned deployments. failovers are opt-in at policy level. we'll show how to pin model versions and rollout policies so no automatic cross-region fallback occurs.
[04:32] Marta: on encryption — are data at rest and in transit encrypted by default? and can we bring our own keys?
[04:39] Priya: data in transit is TLS. at-rest encryption uses cloud provider keys by default, and BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported for private/dedicated. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[04:52] Jordan: routing specifics — if we use privatelink endpoint, how does return traffic flow? does Redwood initiate any connections into our VPC?
[04:59] Priya: with Privatelink, the connection is resolved through an interface endpoint in your VPC; traffic is initiated from you to the service endpoint. Redwood doesn't need to initiate inbound connections to your VPC.
[05:13] Tom: for throughput: our batch workload might hit 300 req/s sustained. how does the private offering handle autoscaling?
[05:20] Priya: dedicated pools are the go-to for predictable throughput — you reserve capacity and autoscale within that pool. for hosted private we have autoscaling but with soft limits and we recommend Dedicated for sustained high throughput.
[05:34] Sam: pricing note — dedicated has a baseline monthly commit but better unit economics at scale.
[05:40] Nadia: compliance — do you have SOC2 docs and pen test results?
[05:44] Alex: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and penetration test summaries. we'll share the package via a protected link.
[05:52] Marta: IP allowlisting — we need to add your egress IPs to our firewall. can you provide a stable list?
[05:58] Alex: yes, we'll provide region-specific egress IP ranges. for Dedicated you can also request a static NAT egress or bring your own egress path if you host in the same VPC.
[06:10] Jordan: if we peer our VPC to Redwood VPC, do we need to open any ports? or is all over TLS 443?
[06:16] Priya: mostly TLS 443 for API calls, but for some internal health checks or control plane we may need additional ports; we'll include a port matrix.
[06:27] Tom: could you outline the pilot? we'd like to validate latency, auth integration, and auditing.
[06:33] Alex: propose a 4-week pilot: week 1: network setup (privatelink or peering) and auth integration; week 2: ingest test prompts and run latency tests; week 3: run a small production-like workload; week 4: review logs, security audit evidence, and economics.
[06:49] Marta: sounds good. for the pilot we need a clear rollback and data deletion plan post-pilot.
[06:55] Priya: we'll provide a cleanup plan and data retention options; for private we can guarantee no retention beyond configured retention windows and show how to purge caches and KV.
[07:07] Nadia: single-sign on and RBAC — do you integrate with our SSO? our SSO is Okta and we enforce SCIM provisioning.
[07:13] Alex: yes Okta SAML/SCIM is supported for Redwood Console for Private. we'll map roles (admin, developer, auditor).
[07:21] Jordan: any limits on model sizes or token quotas in Private?
[07:26] Priya: model size constraints depend on the chosen instance type and quantization profile. we can onboard models up to very large sizes but may recommend quantized variants for cost. we'll give model-specific guidance once you share the expected prompt lengths.
[07:42] Tom: our prompts average 700 tokens, p95 request is 1.2k tokens. any special config?
[07:48] Priya: longer sequences change kernel choices and memory footprint; we'll recommend batch sizes and KV cache settings. we'll also show quantization and batching tradeoffs to keep latency <150ms p95 if possible.
[08:02] Sam: recording note — customer asked about a self-hosted option on-prem for certain tenants. that's a higher tier private option.
[08:09] Tom: yes we might want an on-prem isolated for high-risk data. what's the difference?
[08:14] Priya: on-prem is more of a packaged private deployment with a customer-managed control plane and HSM integration; it requires more ops lift and longer lead time. tradeoff is full isolation and control.
[08:28] Marta: can the private offering integrate with our VPC flow logs and send to our SIEM?
[08:33] Priya: yes we support pushing logs to your S3/Kinesis/Splunk; we'll provide sample config.
[08:40] Jordan: networking gotchas — NAT translation, ephemeral ENI exhaustion, cross-account route table entries; any common pitfalls?
[08:49] Priya: common ones are insufficient IP space for ENIs, forgetting to add route table entries for endpoint ENIs, and not opening required ports for the control plane (if using managed control plane). we include a checklist.
[09:02] Tom: any multi-tenant concerns? we need assurance that a noisy neighbor won't impact our performance in hosted private env.
[09:10] Alex: for dedicated you get isolated capacity; for hosted private we do soft isolation with resource controls and can set conformance tests. if strict isolation is required, dedicated is recommended.
[09:24] Nadia: auditors mandate encryption keys, we need KMS audit logs. can Redwood surface KMS access events?
[09:31] Priya: we can show KMS access logs for customer-managed keys and work with you on the log retention policies.
[09:40] Marta: one more on IP: do you support BYO egress through our NAT gateway instead of Redwood egress?
[09:47] Priya: yes, if you host in the same VPC or have a PrivateLink setup with VPC endpoints, you can route egress through your NAT. for hosted managed egress we provide egress IP ranges instead.
[09:59] Tom: let's talk schedule — timeline for pilot and procurement. we're aiming to have a production readiness decision in 6–8 weeks.
[10:08] Alex: cool, pilot in 1–2 weeks, security review parallel. procurement might take 4–6 weeks after pilot depending on legal.
[10:18] Jordan: legal — any standard SLAs for private/dedicated?
[10:22] Alex: Dedicated comes with SLA options; hosted private has a baseline SLA. we'll include SLA language in the docs.
[10:30] Sam: i'll be point for post-pilot onboarding and can set up a handoff with CSM.
[10:36] Tom: thanks. can you also provide a simple list of ports, sample route entries, and the exact private endpoint DNS names?
[10:44] Priya: yes — we'll send a network matrix and sample terraform snippets in the follow-up.
[10:50] Marta: one oddball question: we use a transit VPC that NATs traffic to the internet through a central egress; if we peered with Redwood, will we need to add routes in the transit VPC?
[11:00] Priya: yes you'll need route table entries and ensure TGW accepts the route to Redwood's VPC; transitive routing might require explicit allowances. we'll put in a TGW checklist.
[11:10] Jordan: do you support IPsec tunnels as an alternative?
[11:14] Priya: yes, we support IPsec for Private in some configurations, usually for on-prem or hybrid. it's heavier but works for strict network isolation.
[11:23] Tom: great. any other compliance certs beyond SOC2?
[11:27] Alex: we have SOC2; PCI support is case-by-case (payments customers), we can discuss controls.
[11:34] Nadia: last question — how do you manage model rollout and rollback if we see regressions in production?
[11:39] Priya: rollouts are configurable: canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous model versions. all controlled via the console or API. for private we can lock rollouts to manual.
[11:52] Tom: perfect. let's recap next steps.

Recap by Alex:
[11:58] Alex: action items — priya will send network diagram and port matrix; i'll send pricing and pilot scope; tom will share topology and list of regions. sam will coordinate pilot dates. we'll aim for pilot kickoff 2025-06-24. any objections?
[12:15] Marta: no objections. thanks everyone.
[12:19] Nadia: thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[12:23] Alex: i'll follow up with links: 1) private endpoints diagram, 2) SOC2 pack link (protected), 3) pilot scope doc.
[12:31] Tom: thanks. bye.
[12:33] (meeting ends)

References shared: "Private endpoints diagram" (link: shared: https://redwood.internal/s/private-endpoints-horizonbridge), "SOC2 pack" (protected link), sample terraform snippets (note in follow-up).

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions on product names (eg Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood dedicated pool' vs 'dedicated pool'); speaker overlap around 06:30 where Jordan and Marta interrupt.
